DEVICE = 'cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'

class InferenceBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_units, d_theta, output_units):
        super(InferenceBlock, self).__init__()
        self.module = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_units, d_theta, bias=True),
            nn.ELU(inplace=True),
            nn.Linear(input_units, d_theta, bias=True),
            nn.ELU(inplace=True),
            nn.Linear(d_theta, output_units, bias=True)
        )

    def forward(self, inps):
        out = self.module(inps)
        return out

class Amortized(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_units=400, d_theta=400, output_units=400):
        super(Amortized, self).__init__()
        self.output_units = output_units
        self.weight_mean         = InferenceBlock(input_units, d_theta, output_units)
        self.weight_log_variance = InferenceBlock(input_units, d_theta, output_units)

    def forward(self, inps):
        weight_mean         = self.weight_mean(inps)
        weight_log_variance = self.weight_log_variance(inps)
        return weight_mean, weight_log_variance


class MLP(nn.Module):
	"""
	Two layer MLP for MNIST benchmarks.
	"""
	def __init__(self, hiddens, config):
		super(MLP, self).__init__()
		self.W1 = nn.Linear(784, hiddens)
		self.relu = nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
		self.dropout_1 = nn.Dropout(p=config['dropout'])
		self.W2 = nn.Linear(hiddens, hiddens)
		self.dropout_2 = nn.Dropout(p=config['dropout'])
		self.post  = Amortized(hiddens, hiddens, hiddens)
		self.prior = Amortized(hiddens, hiddens, hiddens)

	def forward(self, x, task_id=None, post = False, predefined = False):
		x = x.view(-1, 784)
		out = self.W1(x)
		out = self.relu(out)
		out = self.dropout_1(out)
		out = self.W2(out)
		out = self.relu(out)
		out = self.dropout_2(out)
		out_features = self.normalize(out)
		out_mean = torch.mean(out_features, dim=0, keepdim=True)
		if post:
			mu, logvar = self.post(out_mean)
		else:
			mu, logvar = self.prior(out_mean)
		return out_features, mu, logvar

	def normalize(self, x):
		max_val = x.max()
		min_val = x.min()
		return (x - min_val) / (max_val - min_val)

def conv3x3(in_planes, out_planes, stride=1):
	return nn.Conv2d(in_planes, out_planes, kernel_size=3, stride=stride,
					 padding=1, bias=False)


class BasicBlock(nn.Module):
	expansion = 1

	def __init__(self, in_planes, planes, stride=1, config={}):
		super(BasicBlock, self).__init__()
		self.conv1 = conv3x3(in_planes, planes, stride)
		self.conv2 = conv3x3(planes, planes)

		self.shortcut = nn.Sequential()
		if stride != 1 or in_planes != self.expansion * planes:
			self.shortcut = nn.Sequential(
				nn.Conv2d(in_planes, self.expansion * planes, kernel_size=1,
						  stride=stride, bias=False),
			)
		self.IC1 = nn.Sequential(
			nn.BatchNorm2d(planes),
			nn.Dropout(p=config['dropout'])
			)

		self.IC2 = nn.Sequential(
			nn.BatchNorm2d(planes),
			nn.Dropout(p=config['dropout'])
			)

	def forward(self, x):
		out = self.conv1(x)
		out = relu(out)
		out = self.IC1(out)

		out += self.shortcut(x)
		out = relu(out)
		out = self.IC2(out)
		return out


class ResNet(nn.Module):
	def __init__(self, block, num_blocks, num_classes, nf, config={}):
		super(ResNet, self).__init__()
		self.in_planes = nf

		self.conv1 = conv3x3(3, nf * 1)
		self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(nf * 1)
		self.layer1 = self._make_layer(block, nf * 1, num_blocks[0], stride=1, config=config)
		self.layer2 = self._make_layer(block, nf * 2, num_blocks[1], stride=2, config=config)
		self.layer3 = self._make_layer(block, nf * 4, num_blocks[2], stride=2, config=config)
		self.layer4 = self._make_layer(block, nf * 8, num_blocks[3], stride=2, config=config)
		self.hiddens = nf * 8 * block.expansion
		self.post  = Amortized(self.hiddens, self.hiddens, self.hiddens)
		self.prior = Amortized(self.hiddens, self.hiddens, self.hiddens)

	def _make_layer(self, block, planes, num_blocks, stride, config):
		strides = [stride] + [1] * (num_blocks - 1)
		layers = []
		for stride in strides:
			layers.append(block(self.in_planes, planes, stride, config=config))
			self.in_planes = planes * block.expansion
		return nn.Sequential(*layers)

	def forward(self, x, task_id=None, post = False, kernel="rff", predefined=False):
		bsz = x.size(0)
		out = relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x.view(bsz, 3, 32, 32))))
		out = self.layer1(out)
		out = self.layer2(out)
		out = self.layer3(out)
		out = self.layer4(out)
		out = adaptive_avg_pool2d(out, 1)
		out = out.view(out.size(0), -1)
		out_features = normalize(out)
		out_mean = torch.mean(out_features, dim=0, keepdim=True)
		if kernel == "rff":
			if post:
				mu, logvar = self.post(out_mean)
			else:
				mu, logvar = self.prior(out_mean)
			return out_features, mu, logvar
		else:
			return out_features


class ResNetMiniImagenet(nn.Module):
	def __init__(self, block, num_blocks, nf, s, config={}):
		super(ResNetMiniImagenet, self).__init__()
		self.in_planes = nf[0]

		self.conv1 = self._conv7x7(3, nf[0], stride=s[0])
		self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(nf[0])
		self.layer1 = self._make_layer(block, nf[1], num_blocks[0], stride=s[1], config=config)
		self.layer2 = self._make_layer(block, nf[2], num_blocks[1], stride=s[2], config=config)
		self.layer3 = self._make_layer(block, nf[3], num_blocks[2], stride=s[3], config=config)
		self.layer4 = self._make_layer(block, nf[4], num_blocks[3], stride=s[4], config=config)
		self.hiddens = nf[4]
		self.post  = Amortized(self.hiddens, self.hiddens, self.hiddens)
		self.prior = Amortized(self.hiddens, self.hiddens, self.hiddens)

	def _conv7x7(self, in_planes, out_planes, stride=1):
		return nn.Conv2d(in_planes, out_planes, kernel_size=7, stride=stride,
						padding=1, bias=False)
	def _make_layer(self, block, planes, num_blocks, stride, config):
		strides = [stride] + [1] * (num_blocks - 1)
		layers = []
		for stride in strides:
			layers.append(block(self.in_planes, planes, stride, config=config))
			self.in_planes = planes * block.expansion
		return nn.Sequential(*layers)

	def forward(self, x, task_id=None, post = False, kernel="rff", predefined=False):

		x = x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
		bsz, ch, h , w = x.size()
		out = relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x.view(bsz, ch, h, w))))
		out = self.layer1(out)
		out = self.layer2(out)
		out = self.layer3(out)
		out = self.layer4(out)
		out = adaptive_avg_pool2d(out, 1)
		out = out.view(out.size(0), -1)
		out_features = normalize(out, dim=1, p=2)
		out_mean = torch.mean(out_features, dim=0, keepdim=True)
		if kernel == "rff":
			if post:
				mu, logvar = self.post(out_mean)
			else:
				mu, logvar = self.prior(out_mean)
			
			return out_features, mu, logvar
		else:
			return out_features


def ResNet18(nclasses=100, nf=20, config={}):
	net = ResNet(BasicBlock, [2, 2, 2, 2], nclasses, nf, config=config)
	return net

def ResNet18MiniImagenet(nclasses=100, config={}):
	net = ResNetMiniImagenet(BasicBlock, [2, 2, 2, 2], 
					nf=[64, 64, 128, 128, 512], 
					s=[2, 2, 2, 2, 2], 
					config=config)
	return net

def sample(mu, logvar, L, device):
    shape = (L, ) + mu.size()
    eps   = torch.randn(shape).to(device)
    w     = mu.unsqueeze(0) + eps * logvar.exp().sqrt().unsqueeze(0)
    return w

def rand_features(bases, features, bias):
    return math.sqrt(2/bias.shape[0]) * torch.cos(torch.matmul(bases, features) + bias)

def dotp_kernel(feature1, feature2):
    return torch.matmul(feature1, feature2)

def kl_div(m, log_v, m0, log_v0):
    
    v = log_v.exp()
    v0 = log_v0.exp()

    dout, din = m.shape
    const_term = -0.5 * dout * din
    
    log_std_diff = 0.5 * torch.sum(torch.log(v0) - torch.log(v))
    mu_diff_term = 0.5 * torch.sum((v + (m0-m)**2) / v0)
    kl = const_term + log_std_diff + mu_diff_term
    return kl

class AverageMeter(object):
    """Computes and stores the average and current value"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.reset()

    def reset(self):
        self.val = 0
        self.avg = 0
        self.sum = 0
        self.count = 0

    def update(self, val, n=1):
        self.val = val
        self.sum += val * n
        self.count += n
        self.avg = self.sum / self.count

def get_train_loader(dataset, batch_size):
	train_loader = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=batch_size, num_workers=4, pin_memory=True, shuffle=True)
	return train_loader


def get_test_loader(dataset):
	test_loader  = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(dataset,  batch_size=256, shuffle=False, num_workers=4, pin_memory=True)
	return test_loader

def coreset_selection(dataset, coreset_size, dataset_name):
	if 'mnist' in dataset_name:
		targets = dataset.targets
		sample_per_each_class = coreset_size // len(targets.unique())
	else:
		loader = get_test_loader(dataset)
		inputs, targets = iterate_data(loader)
		sample_per_each_class = coreset_size

	idx = []
	for cl in targets.unique():
		cl = cl.item()
		cls_idx = torch.where(targets == cl)[0]
		if len(cls_idx) == 0:
			continue
		cls_idx = cls_idx[torch.randperm(len(cls_idx))[:sample_per_each_class]]
		idx = idx + cls_idx.tolist()

	remained_item = list(set(torch.arange(0, len(targets)).tolist()) - set(idx))
	if 'mnist' in dataset_name:
		train_dataset    = torch.utils.data.dataset.Subset(dataset, remained_item)
		coreset_dataset  = torch.utils.data.dataset.Subset(dataset, idx)
	else:
		train_dataset    = torch.utils.data.dataset.TensorDataset(inputs[remained_item], targets[remained_item])
		coreset_dataset  = torch.utils.data.dataset.TensorDataset(inputs[idx], targets[idx])
	return train_dataset, coreset_dataset

def iterate_data(loader):
    xs,ys = [], []
    for x,y in loader:
        xs.append(x)
        ys.append(y)
    xs = torch.cat(xs, dim=0).squeeze(1)
    ys = torch.cat(ys, dim=0)
    return xs, ys


def get_permuted_mnist(task_id):
	"""
	Get the dataset loaders (train and test) for a `single` task of permuted MNIST.
	This function will be called several times for each task.
	
	:param task_id: id of the task [starts from 1]
	:param batch_size:
	:return: a tuple: (train loader, test loader)
	"""
	
	# convention, the first task will be the original MNIST images, and hence no permutation
	if task_id == 1:
		idx_permute = np.array(range(784))
	else:
		idx_permute = torch.from_numpy(np.random.RandomState().permutation(784))
	transforms = torchvision.transforms.Compose([torchvision.transforms.ToTensor(),
				torchvision.transforms.Lambda(lambda x: x.view(-1)[idx_permute] ),
				])
	mnist_train = torchvision.datasets.MNIST('./data/', train=True, download=True, transform=transforms)
	mnist_test  = torchvision.datasets.MNIST('./data/', train=False, download=True, transform=transforms)
	
	return mnist_train, mnist_test



def get_permuted_mnist_tasks(num_tasks):
	"""
	Returns the datasets for sequential tasks of permuted MNIST
	
	:param num_tasks: number of tasks.
	:param batch_size: batch-size for loaders.
	:return: a dictionary where each key is a dictionary itself with train, and test loaders.
	"""
	datasets = {}
	for task_id in range(1, num_tasks+1):
		train_dataset, test_dataset = get_permuted_mnist(task_id)
		datasets[task_id] = {'train': train_dataset, 'test': test_dataset}
	return datasets


class RotationTransform:
	"""
	Rotation transforms for the images in `Rotation MNIST` dataset.
	"""
	def __init__(self, angle):
		self.angle = angle

	def __call__(self, x):
		return TorchVisionFunc.rotate(x, self.angle, fill=(0,))


def get_rotated_mnist(task_id):
	"""
	Returns the dataset for a single task of Rotation MNIST dataset
	:param task_id:
	:param batch_size:
	:return:
	"""
	per_task_rotation = 10
	rotation_degree = (task_id - 1)*per_task_rotation
	rotation_degree -= (np.random.random()*per_task_rotation)

	transforms = torchvision.transforms.Compose([
		RotationTransform(rotation_degree),
		torchvision.transforms.ToTensor(),
		])

	mnist_train = torchvision.datasets.MNIST('./data/', train=True, download=True, transform=transforms)
	mnist_test  = torchvision.datasets.MNIST('./data/', train=False, download=True, transform=transforms)
	
	return mnist_train, mnist_test



def get_rotated_mnist_tasks(num_tasks):
	"""
	Returns data loaders for all tasks of rotation MNIST dataset.
	:param num_tasks: number of tasks in the benchmark.
	:param batch_size:
	:return:
	"""
	datasets = {}
	for task_id in range(1, num_tasks+1):
		train_dataset, test_dataset = get_rotated_mnist(task_id)
		datasets[task_id] = {'train': train_dataset, 'test': test_dataset}
	return datasets


def get_split_cifar100(task_id, cifar_train, cifar_test):
	"""
	Returns a single task of split CIFAR-100 dataset
	:param task_id:
	:param batch_size:
	:return:
	"""
	

	start_class = (task_id-1) * 5
	end_class = task_id * 5

	targets_train = torch.tensor(cifar_train.targets)
	target_train_idx = ((targets_train >= start_class) & (targets_train < end_class))
	
	targets_test = torch.tensor(cifar_test.targets)
	target_test_idx = ((targets_test >= start_class) & (targets_test < end_class))

	train_dataset = torch.utils.data.dataset.Subset(cifar_train, np.where(target_train_idx==1)[0])
	test_dataset  = torch.utils.data.dataset.Subset(cifar_test, np.where(target_test_idx==1)[0])

	return train_dataset, test_dataset


def get_split_cifar100_tasks(num_tasks):
	"""
	Returns data loaders for all tasks of split CIFAR-100
	:param num_tasks:
	:param batch_size:
	:return:
	"""
	datasets = {}
	
	# convention: tasks starts from 1 not 0 !
	# task_id = 1 (i.e., first task) => start_class = 0, end_class = 4
	cifar_transforms = torchvision.transforms.Compose([torchvision.transforms.ToTensor(),])
	cifar_train = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR100('./data/', train=True, download=True, transform=cifar_transforms)
	cifar_test = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR100('./data/', train=False, download=True, transform=cifar_transforms)
	
	for task_id in range(1, num_tasks+1):
		train_dataset, test_dataset = get_split_cifar100(task_id, cifar_train, cifar_test)
		datasets[task_id] = {'train': train_dataset, 'test': test_dataset}
	return datasets


def get_mini_imagenet_tasks(num_tasks):
	"""
	Returns data loaders for all tasks of split CIFAR-100
	:param num_tasks:
	:param batch_size:
	:return:
	"""
	data_file = './data/MiniImageNet/miniImageNet_full.pickle'
	imagenet_data = _load_miniImagenet(data_file)
	datasets = {}

	imagenet_images = imagenet_data['images']
	imagenet_labels = imagenet_data['labels']
	train_count = 500
	test_count = 100

	
	for task_id in range(1, num_tasks+1):
		start_class = (task_id-1) * 5
		end_class = task_id * 5

		for count, cls in enumerate(range(start_class, end_class)):
			# Load all the examples of this class and split the data in train/ test
			class_indices = np.where(imagenet_labels == cls)[0]
			class_indices = np.sort(class_indices, axis=None)

			# Check if required 600 images per class class are present
			assert(class_indices.shape[0] == 600)

			if count == 0:
				x_train = imagenet_images[class_indices[:train_count]]
				y_train = imagenet_labels[class_indices[:train_count]]
				x_test = imagenet_images[class_indices[train_count:train_count+test_count]]
				y_test = imagenet_labels[class_indices[train_count:train_count+test_count]]
			else:
				x_train = np.concatenate((x_train, imagenet_images[class_indices[:train_count]]), axis=0)
				y_train = np.concatenate((y_train, imagenet_labels[class_indices[:train_count]]), axis=0)
				x_test = np.concatenate((x_test, imagenet_images[class_indices[train_count:train_count+test_count]]), axis=0)
				y_test = np.concatenate((y_test, imagenet_labels[class_indices[train_count:train_count+test_count]]), axis=0)
				
		train_dataset = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(torch.tensor(x_train).float(), torch.tensor(y_train).long())
		test_dataset  = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(torch.tensor(x_test).float(), torch.tensor(y_test).long())
		datasets[task_id] = {'train': train_dataset, 'test': test_dataset}
	return datasets

def _load_miniImagenet(data_file):
	"""
	Load the ImageNet data
	Args:
		data_file    Pickle file containing the miniImageNet data
	"""
	# Dictionary to store the dataset
	dataset = dict()
	IMG_MEAN = np.array((0.406, 0.456, 0.485), dtype=np.float32)
	IMG_STD = np.array((0.225, 0.224, 0.229), dtype=np.float32)

	# Load the whole miniimageNet dataset
	with open(data_file, 'rb') as f:
		data = pickle.load(f, encoding="latin-1")

	X = data['images']
	Y = data['labels']
	# Convert RGB image to BGR and subtract mean
	X = np.array(X, dtype=np.float32)
	X_r, X_g, X_b = np.split(X, 3, axis=3)
	X = np.concatenate((X_b, X_g, X_r), axis=3)
	print(X.min(), X.max())
	# Subtract image mean
	X /= 255.0
	X -= IMG_MEAN
	X /= IMG_STD

	dataset['images'] = X
	dataset['labels'] = Y

	return dataset

def get_benchmark_dataset(args):
	"""
	Returns the benchmark loader which could be either of these:
	get_split_cifar100_tasks, get_permuted_mnist_tasks, or get_rotated_mnist_tasks
	
	:param args:
	:return: a function which when called, returns all tasks
	"""
	if args.dataset == 'perm-mnist' or args.dataset == 'permuted-mnist':
		return get_permuted_mnist_tasks
	elif args.dataset == 'rot-mnist' or args.dataset == 'rotation-mnist':
		return get_rotated_mnist_tasks
	elif args.dataset == 'cifar-100' or args.dataset == 'cifar100':
		return get_split_cifar100_tasks
	elif args.dataset == 'mini-imagenet':
		return get_mini_imagenet_tasks
	else:
		raise Exception("Unknown dataset.\n"+
						"The code supports 'perm-mnist, rot-mnist, and cifar-100.")


def get_benchmark_model(args):
	"""
	Return the corresponding PyTorch model for experiment
	:param args:
	:return:
	"""
	if 'mnist' in args.dataset:
		if args.tasks == 20 and args.hiddens < 256:
			print("Warning! the main paper MLP with 256 neurons for experiment with 20 tasks")
		return MLP(args.hiddens, {'dropout': args.dropout}).to(DEVICE)
	elif 'cifar' in args.dataset:
		return ResNet18(config={'dropout': args.dropout}).to(DEVICE)
	elif 'imagenet' in args.dataset:
		return ResNet18MiniImagenet(config={'dropout': args.dropout}).to(DEVICE)
	else:
		raise Exception("Unknown dataset.\n"+
						"The code supports 'perm-mnist, rot-mnist, and cifar-100.")


time_complexity = AverageMeter()

def train_single_epoch(net, optimizer, loader, coreset_loader, criterion, bias, lmd, gma, bta, args, task_id=None):
	net = net.to(DEVICE)
	net.train()

	coreset_input, coreset_target = iterate_data(coreset_loader)
	coreset_input  = coreset_input.to(DEVICE)
	coreset_target = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(coreset_target, num_classes=10 if "mnist" in args.dataset else 100)
	coreset_target = coreset_target.to(DEVICE).float()
	
	task_acc = AverageMeter()
	task_loss = AverageMeter()

	time_complexity_history = AverageMeter()

	for _, (data, target) in enumerate(loader):
		start_time = benchmarker.time()
		data = data.to(DEVICE)
		target = target.to(DEVICE)
		batch_size = data.shape[0]
		optimizer.zero_grad()
		
		if task_id:
			features_train,   p_mu, p_log_var = net(data, task_id, post = False, predefined=True)
			features_coreset, r_mu, r_log_var  = net(coreset_input, task_id, post = True)
		else:
			features_train,   p_mu, p_log_var = net(data,          post = False, predefined=True)
			features_coreset, r_mu, r_log_var  = net(coreset_input, post = True)

		rs = sample(r_mu, r_log_var, args.d_rn_f, DEVICE).squeeze()


		x_supp_phi_t = rand_features(rs, torch.transpose(features_coreset, 1, 0), bias)
		support_kernel = dotp_kernel(torch.transpose(x_supp_phi_t, 1, 0), x_supp_phi_t)

		alpha = torch.matmul(torch.inverse(support_kernel + (torch.abs(lmd[task_id-1]) + 0.01) * torch.eye(support_kernel.shape[0]).to(DEVICE)), coreset_target) 
		
		x_que_phi_t = rand_features(rs, torch.transpose(features_train, 1, 0), bias)

		cross_kernel = dotp_kernel(torch.transpose(x_supp_phi_t, 1, 0), x_que_phi_t)

		pred = gma[task_id-1] * torch.matmul(cross_kernel.T, alpha) + bta[task_id-1]
		
		end_time = benchmarker.time()

		time_complexity_history.update((end_time - start_time)/batch_size)

		if "cifar" in args.dataset or "mini" in args.dataset:
			t = task_id
			offset1 = int((t-1) * 5)
			offset2 = int(t * 5)
			
			if offset1 > 0:
				pred[:, :offset1].data.fill_(-10e10)
			if offset2 < 100:
				pred[:, offset2:100].data.fill_(-10e10)



		kl_loss = kl_div(r_mu, r_log_var, p_mu, p_log_var)
		
		loss = criterion(pred, target) + args.tau * kl_loss
		task_loss.update(loss.item())

		acc = (pred.argmax(dim=-1) == target).float().mean()
		task_acc.update(acc.item())


		loss.backward()
		optimizer.step()
	
	print(f"Task {task_id} time complexity is {time_complexity_history.avg}")
	global time_complexity
	time_complexity.update(time_complexity_history.avg)

	print(task_acc.avg, task_loss.avg)
	return net


def eval_single_epoch(net, loader, coreset_loader, criterion, bias, lmd, gma, bta, args, task_id=None):
	net = net.to(DEVICE)
	net.eval()

	coreset_input, coreset_target = iterate_data(coreset_loader)
	coreset_input  = coreset_input.to(DEVICE)
	coreset_target = torch.nn.functional.one_hot(coreset_target, num_classes=10 if "mnist" in args.dataset else 100)
	coreset_target = coreset_target.to(DEVICE).float()

	test_loss = AverageMeter()
	correct   = AverageMeter()

	with torch.no_grad():
		for data, target in loader:
			data = data.to(DEVICE)
			target = target.to(DEVICE)
			if task_id:
				features_test,   p_mu, p_log_var = net(data, task_id, post = False)
				features_coreset, r_mu, r_log_var  = net(coreset_input, task_id, post = True)
			else:
				features_test,   p_mu, p_log_var = net(data,          post = False)
				features_coreset, r_mu, r_log_var  = net(coreset_input, post = True)

			rs = sample(r_mu, r_log_var, args.d_rn_f, DEVICE).squeeze()

			x_supp_phi_t = rand_features(rs, torch.transpose(features_coreset, 1, 0), bias)  
			
			support_kernel = dotp_kernel(torch.transpose(x_supp_phi_t, 1, 0), x_supp_phi_t)  

			alpha = torch.matmul(torch.inverse(support_kernel + (torch.abs(lmd[task_id-1]) + 0.01) * torch.eye(support_kernel.shape[0]).to(DEVICE)), coreset_target)
			x_que_phi_t = rand_features(rs, torch.transpose(features_test, 1, 0), bias)

			cross_kernel = dotp_kernel(torch.transpose(x_supp_phi_t, 1, 0), x_que_phi_t)

			pred = gma[task_id-1] * torch.matmul(cross_kernel.T, alpha) + bta[task_id-1]
			target_kernel = dotp_kernel(coreset_target, coreset_target.T)
			target_kernel = 0.99 * (target_kernel + 0.01)
			
			kernel_align_loss = cosine_dist(target_kernel, support_kernel)

			kl_loss = kl_div(r_mu, r_log_var, p_mu, p_log_var)
			
			loss = criterion(pred, target) + args.zeta * kernel_align_loss + args.tau * kl_loss
			
			test_loss.update(loss.item())

			acc = (pred.argmax(dim=-1) == target).float().mean()
			correct.update(acc.item())
	
	return {'accuracy': correct.avg, 'loss': test_loss.avg}


def cosine_dist(a, b):
    a = a.view(1, -1)
    b = b.view(1, -1)
    normalize_a = torch.nn.functional.normalize(a, dim=-1)
    normalize_b = torch.nn.functional.normalize(b, dim=-1)
    return torch.sqrt(torch.sum(torch.multiply(normalize_a, normalize_b)))
llm_extracted_info.experimental_info:
The methodology involves a shared feature extractor (hθ) and task-specific non-parametric classifiers constructed using Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) based on a coreset of training samples stored in an episodic memory. Data-driven and task-adaptive kernels are achieved using Variational Random Features (VRFs), where the random Fourier basis (ω) is a latent variable. This is formulated as a variational inference problem with a variational posterior qφ(ω|Ct) inferred from the coreset and a conditional prior pγ(ω|Dt\Ct) from the task's training data. Both posterior and prior distributions are modeled using amortized multilayer perceptron networks (fφ and fγ).

**Experimental Setup and Settings:**

*   **Feature Extractor (hθ) Architectures:**
    *   **MNIST datasets (`perm-mnist`, `rot-mnist`):** Two-layer MLP with `--hiddens` (default 256) neurons per layer and `--dropout` (default 0.25).
    *   **CIFAR-100 (`cifar-100`):** ResNet18 (with `nf=20`) with `--dropout` (default 0.25).
    *   **Mini-ImageNet (`mini-imagenet`):** ResNet18MiniImagenet (with `nf=[64, 64, 128, 128, 512]` and strides `[2, 2, 2, 2, 2]`) with `--dropout` (default 0.25).
*   **Amortized Networks (fφ, fγ):** Implemented by `Amortized` class, which uses `InferenceBlock`s. Input and output dimensions match the feature extractor's output (`hiddens` for MLP, `nf * 8 * block.expansion` or `nf[4]` for ResNets).
*   **Kernel Type:** `--kernel` is set to `rff` (Random Fourier Features) which is integral to the VRF approach.
*   **Task Management:**
    *   Number of tasks: `--tasks` (default 5).
    *   Episodic memory: A `coreset_dataset` is created for each task using `coreset_selection` with `--core_size` (default 20) samples. `coreset_selection` samples uniformly per class for MNIST and generically for other datasets.
*   **Training Loop:**
    *   Epochs per task: `--epochs-per-task` (default 1).
    *   Batch size: `--batch-size` (default 10).
    *   Optimizer: SGD with learning rate `lr` and momentum 0.8. `lr` is decayed by `gamma` per task: `lr = max(args.lr * args.gamma ** (current_task_id), 0.00005)`.
    *   Learning Rate: `--lr` (default 0.1).
    *   Learning Rate Decay (`gamma`): `--gamma` (default 0.4).
*   **Loss Function (ELBO Maximization):**
    *   Cross-entropy loss (`nn.CrossEntropyLoss`) for the log-likelihood term.
    *   KL divergence between the posterior `qφ(ω|Ct)` (from `r_mu`, `r_log_var` via `net(coreset_input, post=True)`) and the prior `pγ(ω|Dt\Ct)` (from `p_mu`, `p_log_var` via `net(data, post=False)`).
    *   The KL divergence term is weighted by `--tau` (default 0.0001): `loss = criterion(pred, target) + args.tau * kl_loss`.
    *   During evaluation (`eval_single_epoch`), an additional kernel alignment loss (`cosine_dist` between target kernel and support kernel) weighted by `--zeta` (default 0.) is added: `loss = criterion(pred, target) + args.zeta * kernel_align_loss + args.tau * kl_loss`.
*   **Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR) Parameters:**
    *   KRR regularization parameter: `lmd` (initialized to `--lmd` (default 0.1) and is learnable per task).
    *   Scaling factor `gma` (initialized to 1.0, learnable per task).
    *   Bias `bta` (initialized to 0.0, learnable per task).
*   **Variational Random Features (VRFs):**
    *   Size of random feature basis (`ω`): `--d_rn_f` (default 512).
    *   Bias `b` for random Fourier features: `bias = 2 * math.pi * torch.rand(args.d_rn_f, 1).to(DEVICE)`.
    *   `rand_features` function applies the `sqrt(2/M) * cos(ωx + b)` transformation.
*   **Other Settings:**
    *   Random seed: `--seed` (default 1234).
    *   `--predefined` (default True): Influences the prior calculation in `MLP`/`ResNet` models (though in the extracted `forward` method, it doesn't seem to actively change the prior calculation based on its value).
    *   Optional computation of Hessian eigenvalues: `--compute-eigenspectrum` (default False).

new_method.method:
Open Problems: 1. Can on-device continual learners survive with *sub-kilobyte* memories when the data stream is (a) unlabeled, (b) exhibits gradual concept drift and (c) spans several modalities?  
2. How to guarantee both *differential privacy* and *membership-inference resilience* when the same tiny memory is replayed thousands of times?  
3. What is the *joint optimum* of (memory bytes, energy per sample, latency) – i.e. an information-theoretic Pareto frontier – and can a practical system match it across vision, audio and text?  
4. How to make such memories *federatable* without any shared codec or task boundaries while keeping communication <100 B per round?  
5. How can codebooks remain useful when the backbone itself is updated by larger foundation-model checkpoints that arrive intermittently on the device?
Methods: We propose TACO (Task-Agnostic COnstant-memory learning), a successor to ZIPP that pushes the budget down to 512 bytes and adds foundation-model compatibility.
A. Self-Supervised Drift Probes  
• Replace conformal distance with a lightweight contrastive probe trained online; its temperature is used as a proxy for distributional change—works without labels.  
• The probe’s running entropy drives a PID controller that decides whether to recycle, merge or allocate new codes (no manual thresholds).
B. Universal 4-Level Codebook  
• L0: 32 sinusoidal bases (positional) – hard-wired.  
• L1: 128 learned orthogonal vectors shared across modalities (6-bit addresses) stored once per device (≈1 kB Flash).  
• L2: 256 user-specific *delta* codes (8-bit) learned by product quantisation.  
• L3: Event-specific XOR-sketches (24–48 bit) produced by a single pass of locality-sensitive Bloom pooling.  
• A streaming weighted set-cover algorithm guarantees |L2∪L3|≤64 ⇒ total ≤512 B including timestamps.
C. Elastic LoRA Patching  
• Instead of one hyper-decoder, TACO writes LoRA rank-1 patches *directly* into backbone layers; patches are addressed by (L1,L2,L3) triples and applied only if the probe entropy signals relevance.  
• This avoids any extra forward pass even for multi-modal models.
D. Dual-Privacy Guard  
• Gaussian DP on stored statistics (as in ZIPP) *plus* a new randomized response on address bits → provable (ε,δ)-DP *and* membership-inference leakage ≤1 bit.  
• Homomorphic averaging now works on *entropy-weighted* counts so that rare-event information travels faster across peers.
E. Memory–Energy–Accuracy Bound  
• We extend ZIPP’s rate–distortion–forgetting theorem to include energy: E≥Ω(B⁻¹ log²m).  
• Show that LoRA patching makes TACO match the bound within 1.2× on both ARM Cortex-A55 and Pixel TPU-lite.
F. Foundation-Model Sync  
• When a new backbone checkpoint (e.g. MobileViT-L) is pushed, a small adaptor network projects old codes; costs 0.3× original backbone FLOPs once, after which memory resumes at 512 B.
Experimental Setup: Streams & Benchmarks  
Vision: Ego4D-clips (video), ImageNet-1K (224²), and RingCam-360 continuous home-robot feed.  
Audio: LibriSpeech chronological stream + UrbanSound8K online recordings.  
Text: Wikipedia + Reddit Live-feed for masked-LM.  
Hardware:  Cortex-M55 microcontroller (128 kB SRAM), Raspberry-Pi 5, Pixel 8a; energy via INA260 + on-chip PMU counters.  
Baselines: ZIPP (1 kB), DER++, SparCL, KCL, LOC, ULC, and a 512 B oracle.  
Metrics: Avg Acc, BWT, Online mAP (for detection), bytes total, SRAM peak, Joules/sample, latency, ε-DP, MI-attack AUC, comm bytes/round.  
Ablations: probe type, LoRA rank (1–4), Bloom pool size, adaptor frequency, foundation-model swap.  
Robustness: 20 % label noise, adversarial PGD, synthetic gradual drift.
Expected Result: • TACO retains >97 % of joint-training accuracy on ImageNet-1K after 1 000 drift events with exactly 512 B memory (-0.8 % forgetting).  
• Average energy per video frame: 3.1 mJ (-45 % vs SparCL, ‑30 % vs ZIPP).  
• Membership-inference attack success ≤51 % (random) while ε≤0.8.  
• Federated entropy-weighted exchange adds +2.5 % FWT using only 64 B uplink.  
• After swapping MobileViT-S→MobileViT-L, adaptor converges in 180 ms and memory remains at 512 B with <1 % accuracy drop.
Expected Conclusion: TACO shows that *half-kilobyte*, privacy-safe memories are sufficient for unlabeled, multi-modal continual learning on commodity edge hardware—even when the underlying backbone evolves. By unifying self-supervised drift probes, Bloom-pooled sketches and LoRA patching under a strict 512 B contract, it matches new information-theoretic bounds on memory-energy trade-offs and withstands membership attacks. This paves the way for sustainable, always-on learning in wearables, micro-drones and medical implants without cloud dependence.

idea.open_problems:
Catastrophic forgetting is now largely mitigated by memory-replay schemes, but these methods still keep hundreds to tens-of-thousands of raw samples or feature tensors.  This becomes prohibitive when tasks arrive continuously (e.g. lifelong robotics, on-device learning) or when privacy constraints forbid storing original data.  Current compression attempts (e.g. task-free DRO evolution, dataset-distillation, VQ replay, sparsity or orthogonal parameter isolation) solve only part of the puzzle:  • episodic coresets/latent codes are still an order-of-magnitude larger than network weights;  • methods that eliminate memory (orthogonal subspaces, sparsity, UCB) suffer on complex benchmarks such as Split-miniImageNet;  • generative replay needs an extra decoder that itself grows with tasks or drifts.  The key open challenge is designing a CL system that (1) stores 
O(K·d) bytes per task (K≪10, d = feature dim), i.e. far below one image, (2) avoids task labels at test time, and (3) maintains accuracy on high-resolution vision streams.
idea.methods:
Latent-Orthogonal Coresets (LOC)
1. Task-conditioned feature extractor   A backbone fθ (ResNet-18/ViT-Small) is trained continually.  After each mini-batch the penultimate features h∈ℝ^d are orthogonally projected through a small trainable matrix P_t∈ℝ^{d×r} (r≪d, e.g. 8) that is required to be column-orthogonal across tasks (as in ORTHOG-SUBSPACE).  Hence each task occupies its own low-rank slice of feature space.

2. Subspace coreset construction   At task end we run a single pass of randomized SVD on all projected features P_t^⊤h and keep only the first k singular directions (k≤r); we record
   • μ_t ∈ℝ^k       (mean of coefficients)  
   • Σ_t ∈ℝ^{k×k}   (diagonal cov. of coefficients).
These  (μ_t, Σ_t, P_t) triples constitute the Latent Orthogonal Coreset and replace raw data.  Memory per task: k(k+3)d/2 floats ≈ a few KB.

3. On-the-fly pseudo-replay   When a new task τ arrives we sample coefficients z∼𝒩(μ_t,Σ_t) for all previous tasks, recover latent features ĥ=P_t z and mix them with current minibatch features in the loss.  Two options:
   (a) Feature-level replay – ĥ is fed directly to the classifier head; no decoder is needed.
   (b) Optional lightweight decoder gψ (shared across tasks, frozen capacity) trained with a single VAE objective on current task to invert P_t ; used only for logging / qualitative checks.

4. Continual optimization   Backbone weights θ are updated with an A-GEM style constrain: ⟨g_new, g_replay⟩≥0 where g_replay is gradient on LOC samples.  Because ĥ lives in orthogonal subspaces, the projection test is cheap (k·d).

5. Regularizers
   • Orthogonality of {P_t} enforced on Stiefel manifold (as in prior work).
   • Volume-preserving penalty det(Σ_t) ≥ ε to avoid degenerate coresets.
   • Subspace budget scheduler that merges nearest subspaces when #tasks>d/r.

Novelty vs prior work
  – Unlike ER or DRO we store no data, only tiny statistics.
  – Unlike full-generator replay we avoid a growing decoder.
  – Combines orthogonal parameter isolation with a generative coreset in the same latent space, something not explored before.
idea.experimental_setup:
Benchmarks
1. Permuted-MNIST (20 tasks)
2. Split-CIFAR100 (20×5-class)
3. Split-miniImageNet (20×5-class)
4. CORe50 streaming RGB-D (50 objects, 10 sessions) – to test real video stream.

Baselines
  Finetune, ER-Reservoir (500 & 2 000 imgs), DER++, Task-free DRO, ORTHOG-SUBSPACE (no memory), SparCL-DER++, UCB, Kernel CL.

Metrics
  Average Accuracy (AA), Backward Transfer (BWT), Parameter overhead, Bytes per task.  Report accuracy vs memory curve.

Ablations
  • k (1,2,4,8)  • orthogonal vs soft-orthogonal projections  • feature-level vs decoder replay  • merge strategy when tasks>d/r.

Robustness
  – Class-order shuffled five times.
  – Label-noise 20% on half the tasks.
  – Adversarial PGD attack (ϵ=2/255) evaluated on final model.
Hyper-parameters tuned only on first three tasks of each benchmark.
idea.expected_result:
• LOC matches DER++ accuracy on Split-CIFAR100 with ≤128 KB total memory (≈ 50× smaller).
• Outperforms no-memory methods (orthog-subspace, UCB) by +12 % AA on miniImageNet.
• Memory-accuracy Pareto front strictly dominates all baselines; at 0 bytes of raw data LOC retains >80 % of joint-training accuracy on Permuted-MNIST and >60 % on miniImageNet.
• BWT close to 0 (−1 % to −2 %) versus −10 % for fine-tune.
• Computation overhead <15 % compared with ER (due to low-rank sampling and no decoder forward).
• Robustness: accuracy drop under 20 % label noise is half of ER’s drop; adversarial accuracy 3 % higher than ER.
• Ablations show k=4 sufficient; decoder adds <0.5 % accuracy, confirming feature-level replay suffices.

idea.methods:
Ultra-Compressed Task-Agnostic Latent Coresets (ULC)
A. Task-agnostic event detector
   • Maintain an online change-point detector on the cosine distance between incoming mini-batch feature means and the running exponential moving average.
   • A new latent subspace is allocated only when distribution shift is statistically significant, removing the need for task IDs.

B. Hierarchical binary subspace allocator
   • Instead of a dense R∈ℝ^{d×r}, learn a two-level orthogonal decomposition P=[P1|P2], where P1 is shared across all tasks and P2 is an 8-bit product-quantised perturbation chosen from a codebook of 256 bases.
   • The codebook is meta-learned once and frozen; each newly detected task stores only the 1-byte index of its perturbation plus a 16-byte diagonal Σ and 16-byte μ (k=4).
   • Effective memory ≤ 50 bytes / task → <1 KB for 20 tasks.

C. Self-distilled feature regenerator
   • A tiny (≤20 k parameters) hyper-network hϕ takes the 1-byte code and reconstructs P2 on-the-fly, ensuring decoder capacity is constant.

D. Differentially-private statistic noise
   • Apply analytic Gaussian DP noise to (μ,Σ) calibrated so that ε≤1 over the device lifetime.
   • Prove that the privacy cost is independent of the number of replay steps because only the stored tuples are released.

E. Theoretical bound
   • Derive a PAC-Bayes style bound showing that expected forgetting ≤O(‖Σ‖₂ /√m) where m is mini-batch size during replay; bound motivates choosing k.

F. Cross-modal plug-in
   • Show that the same binary-subspace trick plugs into a TinyBERT encoder (d=312) with identical byte budget, enabling multilingual continual learning.

idea.methods:
We call the refined framework ZIPP (Zero-knowledge, Information-optimal, Poly-modal, Persistent).
A. Multi-granular Drift Monitor
  • Continuously computes a conformal‐prediction p-value on the cosine similarity between the current mini-batch and an exponentially decayed reference buffer.
  • When p < 0.05 for G consecutive windows, a *soft event* is raised; its severity controls how many bytes will be allocated (0–3 scale).
B. Hierarchical Codebook with Recycling
  • Level-0: 64 shared orthogonal bases (4-bit addresses) kept in SRAM.
  • Level-1: 256 device-specific perturbations (8-bit addresses) learned once via meta-SGD and stored in Flash (≈ 8 KB total, amortised across all apps).
  • Level-2: For each detected event, store δ-codes = H(X)⊕H(Ŷ) where H(·) is a small locality-sensitive hash of the event’s mean feature; δ is 32–64 bits.
  • Periodic *recycling*: run online K-Medoids in Hamming space; clusters whose centroids differ by <3 bits are merged and their replay weights averaged—guaranteeing total memory ≤1 KB forever.
C. Tiny Hyper-Decoder with Shared LoRA Adapters
  • One 16 k-parameter MLP reconstructs Level-1 codes; Level-2 δ-codes are applied by low-rank (rank = 2) LoRA adapters that piggy-back on the backbone—no extra forward pass.
D. Zero-Knowledge Federated Exchange
  • Devices publish only the Bloom-filtered *indices* of codes plus an additive homomorphic encryption of (μ,Σ). Peers can aggregate encrypted stats to improve their own decoders yet cannot invert another user’s data.
E. Privacy & Optimality Guarantees
  • Differential privacy proved as ε = O(σ⁻¹ log (1/δ)) with σ the Gaussian noise on (μ,Σ); invariant to replay steps.
  • A new rate–distortion–forgetting theorem shows any ε-DP system with budget B bytes and mini-batch size m incurs expected forgetting ≥ Ω(2^{−B}/√m). ZIPP attains the bound up to a log log m factor.
F. Poly-modal Extension
  • The same δ-code mechanism is applied after a 1-D causal ConvNet for audio and a MobileViT-XS for video frames; only the hash function H changes (SimHash for video patches).

idea.methods:
We propose TACO (Task-Agnostic COnstant-memory learning), a successor to ZIPP that pushes the budget down to 512 bytes and adds foundation-model compatibility.
A. Self-Supervised Drift Probes  
• Replace conformal distance with a lightweight contrastive probe trained online; its temperature is used as a proxy for distributional change—works without labels.  
• The probe’s running entropy drives a PID controller that decides whether to recycle, merge or allocate new codes (no manual thresholds).
B. Universal 4-Level Codebook  
• L0: 32 sinusoidal bases (positional) – hard-wired.  
• L1: 128 learned orthogonal vectors shared across modalities (6-bit addresses) stored once per device (≈1 kB Flash).  
• L2: 256 user-specific *delta* codes (8-bit) learned by product quantisation.  
• L3: Event-specific XOR-sketches (24–48 bit) produced by a single pass of locality-sensitive Bloom pooling.  
• A streaming weighted set-cover algorithm guarantees |L2∪L3|≤64 ⇒ total ≤512 B including timestamps.
C. Elastic LoRA Patching  
• Instead of one hyper-decoder, TACO writes LoRA rank-1 patches *directly* into backbone layers; patches are addressed by (L1,L2,L3) triples and applied only if the probe entropy signals relevance.  
• This avoids any extra forward pass even for multi-modal models.
D. Dual-Privacy Guard  
• Gaussian DP on stored statistics (as in ZIPP) *plus* a new randomized response on address bits → provable (ε,δ)-DP *and* membership-inference leakage ≤1 bit.  
• Homomorphic averaging now works on *entropy-weighted* counts so that rare-event information travels faster across peers.
E. Memory–Energy–Accuracy Bound  
• We extend ZIPP’s rate–distortion–forgetting theorem to include energy: E≥Ω(B⁻¹ log²m).  
• Show that LoRA patching makes TACO match the bound within 1.2× on both ARM Cortex-A55 and Pixel TPU-lite.
F. Foundation-Model Sync  
• When a new backbone checkpoint (e.g. MobileViT-L) is pushed, a small adaptor network projects old codes; costs 0.3× original backbone FLOPs once, after which memory resumes at 512 B.

Robustness: 20 % label noise, adversarial PGD, synthetic gradual drift.

By unifying self-supervised drift probes, Bloom-pooled sketches and LoRA patching under a strict 512 B contract, it matches new information-theoretic bounds on memory-energy trade-offs and withstands membership attacks.
